current_episode.title: HOW TO LEVERAGE YOUR CURRENT SKILLS TO SELL BIGGER DEALS

guest.bio_context: Herb Klan studied finance at Penn State and began his career at GE Healthcare in 2010 through their financial management program, spending time in Milwaukee, Salt Lake City, and Chicago before joining GE Corporate's audit staff as a global auditor. After six years in finance and audit, he transitioned into sales at GE Healthcare in 2015, where he spent seven years running the imaging business in Charlotte, North Carolina, before joining Cisco Systems as an account manager managing top ten accounts across diverse industries including manufacturing, entertainment, automotive, fashion, and hedge funds.

pending_qa.q: How should sales professionals approach complex multi-stakeholder deals across different organizational levels?
pending_qa.r: Understanding that you are often dealing with five to ten or even a dozen different customers on one project requires managing the sales process systematically. Herb Klan learned from audit experience that you must first clear findings with financial analysts, then move up through the finance manager, director, and controller before presenting to the CFO. The same principle applies to customer sales: clear the organization at every level, ensure everyone understands what you're proposing and how it impacts them, build groundswell support with no surprises, and by the time the proposal reaches the CEO, everyone has already seen it and the story is clear.

pending_qa.q: What is the primary skill advantage that helps close complex enterprise deals?
pending_qa.r: PowerPoint is Herb Klan's superpower in sales. He can take very complex concepts and boil them down into a one-page, easy-to-read, digestible format that lays out what's in it for the customer, ties objective stakes to financial or operational outcomes, and clearly outlines next steps. This one-page document serves as a ticket to the boardroom and can sell on his behalf as it moves through the organization, controlling messaging and ensuring key points are not lost when he is not present.

pending_qa.q: How does the nature of enterprise IT infrastructure sales differ from transactional capital equipment sales?
pending_qa.r: At GE Healthcare, relationships were fleet-focused and ongoing—managing fleets of cath labs and CT scanners. At Cisco, the network infrastructure is a living, breathing thing requiring the IT team to be on call 24-7, creating much deeper customer relationships. Cisco is the IT infrastructure for routers, switches, wireless access points, data centers (on-premises or cloud), and security. The biggest differences Herb Klan observed in his first 100 days at Cisco involved understanding not just the hardware but where information is stored and how safe the network is, fundamentally changing the depth and frequency of customer engagement.

pending_qa.q: What organizational obstacles typically block priority and adoption of new IT infrastructure solutions?
pending_qa.r: Two main obstacles exist: prioritization of projects on the IT team's already mile-long to-do list, and breaking the status quo when moving from on-premises infrastructure to cloud solutions or adopting more advanced solutions from startups acquired by Cisco. To overcome this, sales professionals should go wide across different functions like marketing, operations, and engineering, tethering solutions to strategic initiatives in those areas so they move up the priority list and network engineers understand why it should be prioritized.

pending_qa.q: What teaching principle separates top-performing sales professionals from average ones?
pending_qa.r: If you can't teach it, you probably don't know it, and if you don't know it, your customer certainly doesn't know it—and if they don't know it, they feel stupid, get defensive, and the sale is done. Taking an educational approach and simplifying the complex is the job of sales. When you put customers in a position of empowerment where they become more of an expert on the project than their boss, that's when people get excited and adoption actually goes through.

pending_qa.q: How can salespeople use analogies and metaphors to explain complex enterprise solutions?
pending_qa.r: PowerPoint combined with metaphors and analogies helps explain complex concepts by tying them to what the customer already knows. Herb Klan frequently uses vehicle purchase analogies, asking customers what they drive and then comparing portfolio options to those vehicles. The goal is to go back to what the customer knows, make the unfamiliar familiar, and present it in formats like one-page summaries that are easy to digest and can be shared through the organization.
